Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments, they helped. Short answers up front, more below:

1) ON24 accepts duplicate RTMP sources if they are sent as separate stream keys (we do not recommend the same stream key twice). For the cleanest failover we suggest: primary RTMP -> ON24 (primary key A), backup RTMP -> ON24 (key B). Your encoder should be able to send both; if sending identical frames to two keys there is no dedup problem on our side.

2) For ON24->Zoom bridging: we recommend duplicate output from the encoder (two RTMP targets). Use separate keys for ON24 and Zoom. If ON24 ingestion fails, the encoder continues to send to Zoom; for registrant passback, ON24 supports a passback URL that can be hit with registrant_id and event_id — you can keep hitting that from your middleware.

3) Registrant tracking & stitching: We suggest using a persistent registrant UUID generated at registration (store in Acme registration form as registrant_uuid). Include that UUID in the encoder metadata via the live_api (or in the stream as SCTE markers if supported). For post-event stitching, export ON24 and Zoom timestamps and use the UUID to merge segments.

4) Recording handoff: ON24 will store the primary recording. If Zoom ends up being the source for some timeframe, you can export the Zoom cloud recording; we provide an API to mark segments with in/out timestamps so your editor can stitch. Expect a small gap (<2s) at cut points if encoder re-initializes.

Attachments: I put a terse 'duplicate stream' diagram and a sample passback endpoint we can use (see attached pdf). We can also do a preflight on Oct 15 at 10:00 PT — Sarah and my engineer will join.

Best,
Sarah
